name: MySQL AB and Sun Microsystems (MySQL's path to Oracle)
origin_detail: MySQL AB was founded in 1995 by Michael Widenius, David Axmark and Allan Larsson; Mårten Mickos became CEO in 2001. Dual HQ in Uppsala, Sweden and Cupertino, California, with about 400 staff in 25 countries, ~70% remote. Sun Microsystems bought it in 2008; Oracle bought Sun in 2010.
openness_notes: MySQL AB sold MySQL under dual licensing: GPL at no charge, or a commercial licence for uses the GPL did not allow (e.g. embedding in closed products), plus support, training and the MySQL Enterprise subscription (Feb 2005). The whole product was OSI-licensed (3). Under Oracle, MySQL Community Server stays GPL while MySQL Enterprise Server adds proprietary plugins on the same codebase: open core (2). Single-vendor governance throughout.

license_history.note: Date MySQL moved to the GPL not given in fetched pages.

license_history.license: Oracle era: Community Server GPLv2; Enterprise Server with proprietary plugins

exit_events.counterparty: Oracle Corporation (via its purchase of Sun)
exit_events.note: Announced 2009-04-20 at $9.50/share cash; about $7.4B (net $5.6B per text, $5.4B per infobox). US approval 2009-08-20; EU in-depth probe focused on MySQL from 2009-09-03; unconditional EU approval 2010-01-21; completed 2010-01-27.

risk_events: 2009-2010: EU in-depth review of Oracle-Sun centred on Oracle controlling MySQL; Widenius's 'Save MySQL!' petition
Forks: MariaDB (2009, active), Drizzle (discontinued), Percona Server, WebScaleSQL (2014, Facebook/Google/LinkedIn/Twitter, abandoned)
robustness: The GPL code was forkable and was forked repeatedly, but MySQL's trademark and main development stay with Oracle, a single vendor with no foundation. Oracle still ships it: MySQL 9.7 LTS (April 2026) and calendar versioning from July 2026.
openness_effect_assessment: GPL dual licensing made MySQL a default database while still letting MySQL AB charge embedders, and supported a roughly $1B sale to Sun in 2008. The risk event was a change of owner, not of licence: Oracle, a direct competitor, inherited MySQL with Sun, prompting an EU in-depth review and the MariaDB fork.
key_takeaway: MySQL is the founding case for this group: a dual-licensed open-source company that sold for about $1B in 2008, then passed to Oracle with Sun in 2010. Ownership change, not relicensing, drove the community fork (MariaDB), whose company later wrote the BSL used in the relicensing wave.
